searchText: b"h sitemap performance delta boruch hashem. blessed is he. the awtsmoos revealed that a truthful map must also arrive in measured time; awtsmoos.com cannot make a crawler wait through one serial http doorway for every branch and call that architecture sublime. measured failure the isolated verifier on port 8899 served /heichelos/sitemap.xml quickly and correctly, proving public heichel enumeration and xml response composition. the first request to /heichelos/ikar/sitemap.xml traversed the ikar series tree using sequential $i.fetchawtsmoos() calls. it remained alive with fresh worker heartbeats but did not produce a response before the test client's explicit 120 second ceiling. measured result: wall time: 120.231 seconds; curl exit code: 28; no response body available to validate; tunnel and verifier process remained alive. interpretation this is an implementation performance defect, not a transport failure and not evidence that the sitemap url policy is wrong. the serial public http traversal is rejected for production sitemap generation. next architecture search before rewriting heichelgraph.js, inspect the canonical in process series helpers and database layout for one of these better vessels: 1. direct series detail helper calls without http re entry; 2. one recursive/tree helper already used by the api; 3. bounded parallel level order reads if only individual series helpers exist; 4. cached sitemap graph only if direct traversal still cannot meet a reasonable response budget. do not increase timeout as the primary fix. do not weaken publication policy. do not emit numeric road aliases.

searchText: b"h sitemap performance fix plan boruch hashem. blessed is he. the awtsmoos has revealed the shorter path beneath the public doorway; awtsmoos.com can read the same canonical series truth in process, without making its own http river circle back through every foyer. proven direct contract api/social/helper/series.js exports getseries(). the public /series/:series/details api route simply calls: getseries({ $i, heichelid, seriesid, withdetails: true }) the helper reads directly from $i.db and returns: prateem; subseries ids; posts object keys/data; id. therefore the sitemap does not need $i.fetchawtsmoos() for series traversal. rewrite boundary rewrite only: heichelos/routes/heichel/sitemap/heichelgraph.js no route shape, xml format, publication policy, or static file changes are part of this performance fix. improved traversal import canonical getseries() directly. traverse breadth first so branch depth stays bounded and understandable. read each current breadth layer in batches with a small concurrency ceiling. keep the visited series set and 49,000 url output ceiling. preserve canonical path rules: heichel root, named series, named posts, never numeric road aliases. treat errored/missing series as empty branches rather than poisoning the whole sitemap. verification 1. whole file readback. 2. node syntax/import and existing helper shape tests. 3. restart only the isolated 8899 verifier because required js modules are cached. 4. measure /heichelos/ikar/sitemap.xml wall time with a 30 second ceiling. 5. require the same canonical/privacy assertions plus xml parse. 6. if still over 30 seconds, inspect db traversal cost before considering any cache.

searchText: b"h sitemap seed map delta boruch hashem. blessed is he. the awtsmoos revealed that a sitemap should open the gate, not rebuild the palace at request time; awtsmoos.com already speaks ordinary server links from chamber to chamber, so the map may stay swift while the crawl remains sublime. measured rejection of deep sitemap traversal both public api recursion and canonical direct db recursion failed response budgets for ikar. the optimized direct helper still produced zero bytes before a 30 second client timeout. after that request, the same verifier was busy enough that even /heichelos/ikar timed out at 12 seconds. therefore synchronous deep sitemap traversal is rejected as operationally unsafe. replacement architecture /heichelos/sitemap.xml becomes a url set containing every public/discoverable heichel root only. this is not a loss of crawlability because the raw heichel html has already been proven to expose ordinary series links, and raw series html has already been proven to expose ordinary child series and stable named post links. the sitemap seeds the public graph; the html graph carries crawlers through it. remove the advertised and routable per heichel recursive sitemap endpoint. remove its graph module rather than leave dead expensive code. mime repair static robots.txt and root sitemap.xml bodies are correct but are served as application/octet stream because the dynamic server's extension map lacks .txt and .xml entries. repair mime typing at the canonical static file map rather than wrapping root files in a new router.
